mainTopic: Several גיטין on one sheet (כלל versus טופס, according to רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש), and two side-by-side גיטין with signatures stretching under both
overview: This amud deals with several גיטין written on one sheet, with the witnesses signing once at the bottom. רבי יוחנן holds that one date for everyone makes the sheet a shared wording (כלל), so the signatures cover all the couples. A separate date for each couple makes each one its own טופס. ריש לקיש is stricter: only a joint line, 'We, so-and-so and so-and-so, divorced our wives', makes a כלל. רבי אבא challenges רבי יוחנן twice, and both challenges are answered: the connecting ו ('and') answers the first, and identical dates ('On Sunday, on Sunday') answer the second. רבינא then challenges ריש לקיש with 'וכתב לה' and with the case of two slaves, and both challenges are answered. Next the גמרא brings a ברייתא supporting each side and explains how the second one fits ריש לקיש. Finally, a new משנה discusses two גיטין side by side with Hebrew and Greek signatures stretching under both. The גמרא explains why a stretched signature cannot be split to make both גיטין valid.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: only a truly joint wording counts as a כלל
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש holds that even with one date for all couples, each divorce is still a separate טופס. A כלל exists only when all the husbands are written as one group: 'We, so-and-so and so-and-so, divorced our wives.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if one date was written for all of them, it is still a separate טופס. So what does a כלל look like? Where he wrote: 'We, so-and-so and so-and-so, have divorced our wives so-and-so and so-and-so.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes ריש לקיש's opinion, which disagrees with רבי יוחנן about what counts as a shared wording (כלל).
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, a single shared date is enough to tie all the divorces together. ריש לקיש says a shared date is not enough, because each divorce sentence still stands alone. Only one sentence with a plural subject ('we divorced our wives') truly joins them, so the witnesses' signatures clearly cover everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: The date written in the גט
A separate, self-contained wording for each couple
One joint wording that includes all the couples together
What are the circumstances? What does it look like?
So-and-so (a man) and so-and-so (a woman)

steps.confusionAlert: This line begins in the middle of ריש לקיש's statement. Its first half, 'רבי יוחנן says one date for all is a כלל', comes just before this section.

phrases.english: Even if there is one date for all of them
it is also a separate formula.
Rather, what is the case of a general wording?
Where he wrote: 'We, so-and-so and so-and-so,
have divorced our wives so-and-so and so-and-so.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ זְמַן אֶחָד לְכוּלָּן נָמֵי הָוֵי טוֹפֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to ריש לקיש, one date is not enough to make a כלל. Only a joint plural wording ('we divorced our wives') makes a כלל.

steps.title: רבי אבא: maybe the witnesses signed only for the last couple
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא challenges רבי יוחנן. Even with one date, maybe the witnesses meant to sign only for the last divorce written right above them. He supports this worry from a ברייתא that disqualifies a גט when the witnesses signed under a greeting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא objects: According to רבי יוחנן, who says one date for all is a כלל, we should worry that when the witnesses signed, they signed only for the last one! Isn't it taught: if witnesses are signed under a greeting in a גט, it is invalid, because we worry they signed only on the greeting?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא attacks רבי יוחנן's view that one date makes everything a כלל. He brings a ברייתא to show that we worry witnesses signed only for whatever is written right above their names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, a greeting ('send regards') was written after the גט, and the witnesses signed below it. We worry they were only signing on the greeting, so the גט is invalid. רבי אבא compares the case: the last couple's divorce is like that greeting, so maybe the signatures cover only that last couple.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it; he raises a strong challenge
We should be concerned
On the last one
Isn't it taught in a ברייתא?
A greeting; asking about someone's well-being
We are concerned

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba objects to this:
According to Rabbi Yoḥanan, who says
one date for all of them is a general wording,
let us worry that perhaps when the witnesses signed,
phrases.notes: Some versions say חָתְמוּ, in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is חֲתִימִי. Both mean 'signed'.

phrases.english: it was only for the last one that they signed!
Isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
If witnesses are signed under a greeting
in a bill of divorce, it is invalid,

phrases.aramaic: חָיְישִׁינַן שֶׁמָּא עַל שְׁאֵילַת שָׁלוֹם חָתְמוּ?!
phrases.english: because we worry they perhaps signed only on the greeting?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from ריש לקיש's view to challenge רבי יוחנן's definition of a כלל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that one date for all the couples makes it a כלל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא about the greeting shows we worry the witnesses signed only for the text right above them. So even with one date, the signatures may cover only the last couple.

steps.title: The 'ו' (and) connects everything together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with רבי אבהו's report from רבי יוחנן. A greeting written as 'Ask' is invalid, but 'And ask' is valid, because the 'and' links it to the גט. Likewise, רבי יוחנן's כלל case is one written 'so-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't it said about that ברייתא: רבי אבהו said, 'It was explained to me by רבי יוחנן himself: if it says "Ask", it is invalid. If it says "And ask", it is valid.' Here too, it is a case where it is written: 'So-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן by showing that the ברייתא only disqualifies a greeting that stands apart from the גט. When the word 'and' connects the parts, the witnesses' signatures cover everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letter ו ('and') shows that the greeting continues the גט, so the witnesses signed on the whole thing. רבי יוחנן's case of one date is therefore one where each divorce is linked with 'and'. Because of that link, the signatures cover every couple, not just the last one.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated about it (a later explanation of the ברייתא)
It was explained to me personally
'Ask' (send regards), a separate sentence
'And ask', connected to what came before
Valid

steps.whatToRemember: The connecting ו ('and') turns separate pieces into one continuous text, so the witnesses' signatures cover all of it.

phrases.english: Wasn't it stated about it:
Rabbi Abbahu said,
It was explained to me
by Rabbi Yoḥanan himself:
'Ask' is invalid,
'And ask' is valid;
here too, it is where it is written in it:
'So-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבא's challenge by narrowing both the ברייתא and רבי יוחנן's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is limited, and רבי יוחנן's case is set in a specific wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any text written above the signatures could be the only thing the witnesses meant to sign.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the parts are joined with ו ('and'), the signatures cover all of them. רבי יוחנן's כלל is written that way.

steps.title: Why call it a טופס problem? It was written by day and signed at night
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge to רבי יוחנן. If each couple has its own date, why say the problem is that it is a separate טופס? The earlier couples' גיטין are already invalid because the signing date does not match the writing date, like a גט written by day and signed at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: according to רבי יוחנן, who says a date for each one is a טופס, why specifically say it is because of טופס? Derive it from the fact that it is like a גט written during the day and signed at night!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא raises a second challenge to רבי יוחנן. He questions the reason רבי יוחנן gives when each couple has its own date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each divorce has a different date and the witnesses sign once at the end, they signed on the last date. So for the earlier couples, the signing date does not match the date written in their גט. That is already a known reason for invalidity (נכתב ביום ונחתם בלילה), so why give the טופס reason?

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (introduces another challenge)
Why specifically this reason?
Derive it instead from (a simpler reason)
Written during the day and signed at night, so signed on a different date, which makes a גט invalid

steps.whyThisMatters: The next step answers this. It shows why רבי יוחנן needs the טופס reason even though a date problem might seem to exist.

phrases.english: And furthermore, according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, who says
a date for each one is a separate formula:
why is it specifically because of a separate formula?
Derive it instead from the fact that it is
written during the day and signed at night!
phrases.notes: In Jewish law the date changes at nightfall, so 'at night' means a different date from when it was written.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דְּאָמַר זְמַן לְכׇל אֶחָד – זֶהוּ טוֹפֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, a second, separate challenge to רבי יוחנן is raised.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reason (טופס) for invalidating the earlier couples when each couple has its own date
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The witnesses signed on the last date, so the earlier גיטין were signed on a different date from the one written in them. That makes them invalid already, so the טופס reason seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Every couple's line has the same date
steps.stepSummary: מר קשישא בריה דרב חסדא reports that רבי יוחנן's case is one where each couple's line says 'On Sunday', so every date is the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר קשישא son of רב חסדא told רב אשי: In the name of רבי יוחנן, we explain that the case is where each line says 'On Sunday, on Sunday.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 4. Each couple does get its own date, but every date is the same day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 asked why רבי יוחנן blames a separate טופס when the earlier couples' dates should not match the signing. The answer is that every line repeats the same date, 'On Sunday'. So there is no date mismatch, and the only remaining problem is that each line is its own טופס.

keyTerms.meaning: מר קשישא, son of רב חסדא, an אמורא
We say it in the name of (a tradition we have)
On the first day of the week (Sunday)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר קַשִּׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Mar Kashisha, son of Rav Chisda, said to Rav Ashi:
This is how we say it in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
It is a case where it is written in them:
"On Sunday, on Sunday."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 4 by redefining רבי יוחנן's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא): each line has its own date, but all the dates are identical.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Separate dates for each couple would make the earlier גיטין invalid because their dates would not match the signing.
steps.terutzMaskana: All the dates are the same day, so there is no mismatch. The only problem is that each line is a separate טופס.

steps.title: A shared line seems to divorce two women with one גט
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי: by ריש לקיש, a כלל is written 'We, so-and-so and so-and-so, divorced our wives.' But then two women are divorced with one גט, and the תורה says 'וכתב לה', meaning for her alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: ריש לקיש says that even one date for all of them is still a separate טופס, and a כלל is only when it says 'We, so-and-so and so-and-so, divorced our wives so-and-so and so-and-so.' But then two women are divorced with one גט, and the תורה said 'and he shall write for her', not for her and another woman!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks ריש לקיש's description of a valid כלל. That wording seems to break a basic Torah rule about גיטין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said the only true כלל is one line naming all the husbands and wives together. But such a line is one גט for several women. The פסוק 'וכתב לה' teaches that a גט must be written for one specific woman, not shared with another.

keyTerms.meaning: A general, shared wording that covers all the couples together
A separate formula; here, a separate divorce text for one couple
'And he shall write for her', the פסוק showing a גט is for one woman
Her fellow woman (another woman)

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge is aimed at ריש לקיש's version of a כלל, not at רבי יוחנן's.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
According to Reish Lakish, who says:

phrases.aramaic: זְמַן אֶחָד לְכוּלָּן נָמֵי טוֹפֶס הָוֵי;
phrases.english: Even one date for all of them is still a separate formula;
and what is the case of a general wording?
Where it is written like this:
"We, so-and-so and so-and-so, have divorced
our wives so-and-so and so-and-so";

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצְאוּ שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים מִתְגָּרְשׁוֹת בְּגֵט אֶחָד,
phrases.english: so two women turn out to be divorced with one bill of divorce,
and the Torah said: "And he shall write for her":
and not for her and for her fellow woman!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי, לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from defending רבי יוחנן to challenging ריש לקיש's definition of a כלל from Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's definition of a valid כלל ('We, so-and-so and so-and-so, divorced our wives').
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single shared line would be one גט for several women, which violates 'וכתב לה' (written for her alone).

steps.title: After the shared line, each couple is written separately
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that after the shared opening, the scribe went back and wrote each couple separately: 'So-and-so divorced so-and-so, and so-and-so divorced so-and-so.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he then went back and wrote: 'So-and-so divorced so-and-so, and so-and-so divorced so-and-so.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבינא's challenge. The shared line is followed by a separate line for each couple.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general line ties everything together into a כלל, so the witnesses' signatures cover all of it. Then each couple gets its own line, so every woman has her own divorce written specifically for her. This satisfies 'וכתב לה'.

keyTerms.meaning: He then went back and wrote
Divorced

phrases.english: Because he then went back and wrote:
"So-and-so divorced so-and-so,
and so-and-so divorced so-and-so."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the case: the shared line is followed by a separate line for each couple.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כלל is only one shared line, so several women are divorced by one גט.
steps.terutzMaskana: The shared line links everything for the witnesses, and the separate lines give each woman her own גט.

steps.title: One document frees two slaves together
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks how this differs from a ברייתא where a man writes all his property to his two slaves. They acquire it and free each other, so one document seems to work for two people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: How is this different from what is taught in a ברייתא: one who writes all his property to his two slaves, they acquire it and free each other?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict the rule that one document cannot serve two people. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each slave is part of the master's property, so when they acquire everything together, each slave owns half of the other. One document ends up freeing both slaves. Since freeing slaves is compared to divorce, this suggests one גט could divorce two women, against 'וכתב לה'.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difference? (a challenge asking why two cases are treated differently)
It is taught in a ברייתא
His property
His slaves
They free (set free from slavery)

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
And how is this different from what is taught in a baraita:
One who writes all his property to his two slaves:
they acquire it, and they free each other?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule from Step 6 that one document cannot serve two people, using a parallel case about freeing slaves.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle that one גט cannot be used for two women ('ולא לה ולחברתה').
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, one document frees two slaves. Since freeing slaves is compared to divorce, one document should be able to divorce two women too.

steps.title: The slaves case was about two separate documents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers רבינא: the ברייתא about the two slaves was already explained as a case with two separate documents, so it does not show that one document can work for two people.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we already explain that ברייתא as talking about two documents?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 8. It says the slaves case is no proof, because there each slave got his own document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא thought the slaves case showed one document freeing two people. The גמרא recalls that it already explained that case as two separate documents, one for each slave, given at the same moment. So the rule of 'וכתב לה', one document for one person, is not broken.

keyTerms.meaning: We explained it as / we set it up as (a specific case)
Documents

phrases.english: But didn't we establish it
phrases.notes: This points back to an earlier explanation of the ברייתא about the master who wrote his property to his two slaves.

phrases.english: as a case of two documents?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's comparison in Step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The slaves case shows one document can work for two people.
steps.terutzMaskana: The slaves case had two documents, so it does not compare to one גט for two women.

steps.title: There are ברייתות supporting each side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that there is a ברייתא supporting רבי יוחנן and also one supporting ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רבי יוחנן, and a ברייתא was taught that agrees with ריש לקיש.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא announces that each opinion has a supporting ברייתא, and then it will quote them one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש was defended with logic. Now the גמרא says each side also has an earlier source behind it. So neither opinion will be thrown out.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
In agreement with him

phrases.english: It is taught in agreement with Rabbi Yoḥanan,
it is taught in agreement with Reish Lakish.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The challenges are over, and the גמרא now moves to supporting sources for both opinions.
steps.raayaObject: Both רבי יוחנן's and ריש לקיש's positions
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתות, quoted in the next steps

steps.title: Five couples with one shared date: all are divorced
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן begins: if five men divorce in one document with one date for everyone and the witnesses sign at the bottom, all the גיטין are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught in agreement with רבי יוחנן: five men wrote in one גט, 'So-and-so divorces so-and-so, and so-and-so divorces so-and-so, and so-and-so divorces so-and-so,' with one date for all of them and the witnesses signed below. All of them are valid, and the document must be handed to each woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting the ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן. Its first case: one shared date means the whole page is one document, so every couple is divorced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because there is only one date, nothing splits the page into parts. The witnesses at the bottom therefore count for every couple listed. The document still has to be given to each woman, since each one must receive her גט.

keyTerms.meaning: The date written in the document
Below, at the bottom of the document
Valid
And it must be given

phrases.english: It is taught in agreement with Rabbi Yoḥanan:
Five men who wrote in the bill of divorce:
'So-and-so divorces so-and-so,'
'and so-and-so so-and-so, and so-and-so so-and-so,'
and one date for all of them,
and the witnesses signed below –
all of them are valid,
and it must be given to each and every one of the women.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: חֲמִשָּׁה שֶׁכָּתְבוּ בְּתוֹךְ הַגֵּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins quoting the ברייתא that was announced as supporting רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the five men who wrote one גט

steps.title: A separate date for each couple: only the last is divorced
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if each couple has its own date and the witnesses sign below, only the couple whose line is read together with the signatures is divorced. רבי יהודה בן בתירא says it depends on whether there is empty space between the lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is a date for each one and the witnesses signed below, the one that the witnesses' signatures are read with is valid. רבי יהודה בן בתירא says: if there is space between them, it is invalid, and if not, it is valid, because the date does not separate them.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the part of the ברייתא that matches רבי יוחנן. Separate dates make each couple's line its own document, so only the line right above the witnesses counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said each couple with its own date is a separate טופס, so the witnesses only cover the last one, and this ברייתא says the same thing. רבי יהודה בן בתירא disagrees: a date alone does not split the document. Only empty space between the lines makes the earlier couples' גיטין invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Read together with it, meaning the signatures connect to that line
Empty space
Invalid
Separates them

steps.whatToRemember: One shared date: all the couples are divorced. A date for each couple: according to the תנא קמא, only the couple next to the signatures is divorced. רבי יהודה בן בתירא says only empty space splits the document, not the dates.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Invalid' in רבי יהודה בן בתירא's words means invalid for the earlier couples. The last couple, right above the signatures, is still divorced.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the earlier source behind רבי יוחנן's rule that separate dates turn each couple into its own טופס.

phrases.english: If there is a date for each and every one
and the witnesses signed below –
the one that the witnesses' signatures are read with is valid.
phrases.notes: That's the last couple, whose line sits right above the signatures.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:
If there is space between them, it is invalid,
and if not, it is valid;
because a date does not separate them.

steps.triggerLanguage: זְמַן לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד וְהָעֵדִים מִלְּמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the case of separate dates, which is the case רבי יוחנן ruled on.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that separate dates make each couple a separate טופס
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second clause of the ברייתא (את שהעדים נקראים עמו כשר)

steps.title: A ברייתא supporting ריש לקיש: a general opening line makes all valid
steps.stepSummary: Five men write one document. It opens with a general line ('we have divorced our wives'), then lists each couple, with one date at the end and the witnesses signing below. All the גיטין are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports ריש לקיש: If five men wrote a general line in the גט, 'We, so-and-so and so-and-so, have divorced our wives so-and-so and so-and-so; so-and-so divorced so-and-so, and so-and-so divorced so-and-so,' with one date for all and the witnesses signing below, then all of them are valid, and the document must be given to each woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the promised ברייתא that supports ריש לקיש. Its first case is a document that opens with one general line covering all five couples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is the כלל, the opening line that groups all the men together in one sentence. Because of that shared opening, the one date and the witnesses at the bottom cover everyone, so every גט is valid. The ברייתא points to the כלל as what makes them all valid, which fits ריש לקיש: without it, each separate line would stand on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא teaches in line with his view (a supporting source)
A general statement; here, one opening line that includes everyone
So-and-so (man) / so-and-so (woman), a placeholder for real names
It must be handed to each and every woman

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא in line with ריש לקיש:
Five men who wrote a general line in the גט:
"We, so-and-so and so-and-so,
have divorced our wives so-and-so and so-and-so;
so-and-so divorced so-and-so,
and so-and-so divorced so-and-so";
and there is one date for all of them,
and the witnesses signed below:
all of them are valid,
and it must be given to each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 10 announced supporting ברייתות for both sides. Steps 11-12 gave רבי יוחנן's, and this step gives ריש לקיש's.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's position that separate lines in one document need something tying them together to count as one valid document
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about five men who wrote a כלל in one גט

steps.title: Separate dates split the document; רבי מאיר says space doesn't matter
steps.stepSummary: If each couple has its own date and its own space, only the line read together with the witnesses is valid. רבי מאיר says even with no space, the upper ones are invalid because the date cuts them off.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is a date for each one and a space for each one, and the witnesses sign below, only the one the witnesses are read with is valid. רבי מאיר says: even if there is no space between them, the others are invalid, because the date separates them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second case: now each couple's line has its own date. This splits the document into separate pieces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A date usually marks the end of a document, so a date after each couple's line closes that piece off. The witnesses at the bottom then only connect to the last piece, the one 'read with' their signatures. רבי מאיר adds that empty space is not needed for this split; the date alone is enough to cut the lines apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Empty space between the written lines
Read together with it (the witnesses' signatures connect to that line)
Separates them / cuts them off from each other

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 12. There, רבי יהודה בן בתירא made the space matter. Here, רבי מאיר says the date alone separates them, even without any space.

phrases.english: A date for each and every one,
and a space for each and every one,
and the witnesses signed below:
the one that the witnesses are read with is valid.
רבי מאיר says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רֶיוַח בֵּינֵיהֶם –
phrases.english: Even if there is no space between them,
it is invalid, because the date separates them.

steps.triggerLanguage: זְמַן לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד, וְרֶיוַח לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a second case, contrasting one shared date with separate dates.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's view that separate lines can count as separate documents
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second half of the same ברייתא, including רבי מאיר's opinion

steps.title: Why does ריש לקיש need separate dates?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to ריש לקיש, why does the ברייתא talk specifically about separate dates? He holds that even one shared date still leaves each line as its own separate טופס.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to ריש לקיש, why does the ברייתא specifically mention a date for each one? Didn't he say that even with one date for all of them, each line is still a separate טופס?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how the ברייתא fits ריש לקיש. It seems to say more than ריש לקיש needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's own rule is that even with one date for everyone, each 'so-and-so divorced so-and-so' line counts as its own separate piece. If so, separate dates should not be needed to split the document. So why did the ברייתא need separate dates to make the upper lines invalid?

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically? (why mention this exact detail?)
A separate written form or unit; here, each line counts as its own piece of writing
Also / too

phrases.english: And according to ריש לקיש,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אִירְיָא זְמַן לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד?
phrases.english: why specifically a date for each and every one?
Didn't he say:

phrases.aramaic: זְמַן אֶחָד לְכוּלָּן נָמֵי טוֹפֶס הָוֵי!
phrases.english: even one date for all of them is also a separate טופס!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מַאי אִירְיָא זְמַן לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the second case of the ברייתא (step 14) fits ריש לקיש's own rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that this ברייתא supports ריש לקיש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ריש לקיש says one shared date already leaves each line separate, so the ברייתא's need for separate dates seems to go against his rule.

steps.title: A general opening line ties them together, so only separate dates split them
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש's rule applies only when the couples were not joined from the start. Here a general opening line joined them, so they stay together unless separate dates divide them.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule applies where he did not merge them from the beginning. But here, where he merged them from the beginning, if the date splits them, yes, they are separate; if not, no, they are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by limiting ריש לקיש's rule to documents without a general opening line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the document just lists 'so-and-so divorced so-and-so' line after line, each line is its own טופס even with one date. But the כלל at the start ('we have divorced our wives') joins everyone into one document. Once they are joined, only something strong like a separate date can split them, which is why the ברייתא needed separate dates.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply (only) to... (a limiting phrase)
He merged them / joined them together
From the beginning / at the outset
Splits / divides

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש: separate lines in one גט are separate pieces, and only the last one is valid. But if a general opening line (כלל) joins all the couples, they all stay valid together unless a separate date for each one splits them.

phrases.english: These words apply
where he did not merge them from the beginning;
but here, where he merged them from the beginning,
if the date splits them, yes, they are separate;
if not, no, they are not.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלָא עָרְבִינְהוּ מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 by separating a document that has a כלל from one that does not.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases (with a general opening line vs. without one)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש's rule seems to make every line separate even with one date, so separate dates should not matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: ריש לקיש's rule applies only without a כלל. With a כלל joining them, only separate dates split them, so the ברייתא fits ריש לקיש.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that ריש לקיש's view depends on how the document begins, and this is what lets the ברייתא count as support for him.

steps.title: Two side-by-side divorce documents with Hebrew and Greek signatures
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that when two pairs of witnesses (one Hebrew, one Greek) sign across two adjacent גיטין, the גט that the first pair's names are read with is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two גיטין were written next to each other. Two Hebrew witnesses signed, and their names run from under this one to under that one. Two Greek witnesses also signed, and their names run from under this one to under that one. The גט that the first witnesses are read together with is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic: two גיטין side by side, with signatures stretching underneath both. It tells us which of the two is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hebrew is written right to left, so a Hebrew signature starts under the right-hand גט. Greek is written left to right, so it starts under the left-hand גט. The גט where the first pair of witnesses begins is the one they are seen as signing. The other גט is not considered signed.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (here, a new one begins)
One next to the other
Witnesses who sign in Hebrew (right to left)
Witnesses who sign in Greek (left to right)
Are read together with it, meaning their signature clearly belongs to that document

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think both גיטין are valid just because signatures appear under both. A signature belongs to the גט where it begins, following the direction of that language's writing.

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי גִיטִּין שֶׁכְּתָבָן זֶה בְּצַד זֶה,
phrases.english: Two bills of divorce that were written one next to the other,
and two Hebrew witnesses
extend from underneath this one to underneath that one,
and two Greek witnesses
extend from underneath this one to underneath that one –

phrases.aramaic: אֶת שֶׁהָעֵדִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים נִקְרָאִין עִמּוֹ, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: the one with which the first witnesses are read is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי גִיטִּין שֶׁכְּתָבָן זֶה בְּצַד זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about two גיטין side by side, after the previous discussion of several couples in one document.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When signatures run across two adjacent גיטין, only the גט where the first pair of witnesses begins is valid.

steps.title: Alternating Hebrew and Greek witnesses make both documents invalid
steps.stepSummary: If the witnesses alternate, Hebrew then Greek then Hebrew then Greek, both גיטין are invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one witness signed in Hebrew and one in Greek, and again one in Hebrew and one in Greek, with the signatures stretching from under this גט to under that one, both גיטין are invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case, where the languages alternate from line to line. Here neither גט is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With alternating languages, the first Hebrew witness starts under one גט and the first Greek witness starts under the other. So no single גט has a proper pair of first witnesses. That is why both are invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: One witness
Both are invalid

steps.whatToRemember: Same language for the first pair means one גט is valid. Mixed languages in the first pair means both גיטין are invalid.

phrases.aramaic: עֵד אֶחָד עִבְרִי וְעֵד אֶחָד יְוָנִי,
phrases.english: One Hebrew witness and one Greek witness,

phrases.aramaic: וְעֵד אֶחָד עִבְרִי וְעֵד אֶחָד יְוָנִי,
phrases.english: and one Hebrew witness and one Greek witness,
extending from underneath this one to underneath that one –
both are invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵד אֶחָד עִבְרִי וְעֵד אֶחָד יְוָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A contrasting case to step 17: mixed languages instead of matching pairs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When Hebrew and Greek signatures alternate across two adjacent גיטין, both are invalid.

steps.title: Why not split one signature to validate both documents?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the stretched signature cannot count for both גיטין: "ראובן" under one, and "בן יעקב עד" under the other, since a later משנה accepts "son of so-and-so, witness" as a valid signature.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let this גט be made valid by "ראובן," and that גט by "son of יעקב, witness"! After all, we learned that a signature reading "son of so-and-so, witness" is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first case of the משנה. It asks why only one גט is valid when the long signature could be split in two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each signature stretches under both גיטין. The part under one could be "ראובן" and the part under the other could be "בן יעקב עד." A later משנה says "son of so-and-so, witness" is a valid signature by itself, so it seems both גיטין should be valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be made valid
For we learned (in a משנה)
"Son of so-and-so, witness": a signature that gives only the father's name
Valid

phrases.english: GEMARA:
But let this one be validated by "Reuven,"
and that one by "son of Yaakov, witness,"
for we learned:
phrases.notes: This refers to a משנה that comes a bit later, on 87b.

phrases.english: "Son of so-and-so, witness" is valid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 17 that only one גט is valid.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that only the גט where the first witnesses begin is valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A later משנה accepts "son of so-and-so, witness" as a full signature. So the half of the signature under the second גט should count for that גט, making both valid.

steps.title: The signature splits in the middle, so neither half stands alone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is where "ראובן בן" is under the first גט and "יעקב עד" is under the second, so neither half is a complete signature.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where "ראובן son of" is written on the first one, and "יעקב, witness" on the latter one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining exactly where the signature breaks between the two גיטין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The break comes after the word "son of," not before it. So the second גט only has "יעקב עד," which is not the accepted form "son of so-and-so, witness." The way the words are split shows it is one signature belonging only to the first גט.

keyTerms.meaning: Where it is written
On the first one
On the latter one

steps.whatToRemember: At this stage, the גמרא places the split at "ראובן בן" / "יעקב עד" to show the second גט lacks a complete signature. Step 21 challenges this, and Steps 22-23 give the final answers.

phrases.english: Where "Reuven son of" is written on the first,
and "Yaakov, witness" on the latter.
phrases.notes: The גמרא's point here is that "son of" is on the first side. The next step asks whether "יעקב עד" could still count as a short signature.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: defines exactly where the signature breaks.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The signature might split as "ראובן" / "בן יעקב עד," giving each גט a valid signature.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of a split as "ראובן בן" / "יעקב עד," so the second גט has no valid signature.

steps.title: Why not let each half of the signature count for a different גט?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 20. Let "ראובן בן" validate the first גט and "יעקב עד" validate the second, since the משנה rules that "So-and-so, witness" is a valid signature.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let this גט be made valid by "Reuven son of," and let that גט be made valid by "יעקב witness." After all, we learned in the משנה that a signature reading "So-and-so, witness" is valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. Even with the signature split as "ראובן בן" and "יעקב עד", each piece still looks like it could work as a signature on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said neither half is a complete signature. But "יעקב עד" looks just like the case the משנה approves: a name plus the word "witness", with no father's name. So the second גט should be valid on the strength of "יעקב עד", and the first גט should be valid through "ראובן בן".

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be made valid
We learned (in a משנה)
"So-and-so, witness": a signature with a name but no father's name
Valid

phrases.english: But let this one be validated by "Reuven son of,"
phrases.notes: "This one" is the first גט, the one with the start of the stretched signature under it.

phrases.english: and let that one be validated by "Yaakov witness,"
for we learned:
"So-and-so, witness" is valid!
phrases.notes: This is the same משנה mentioned in Step 19, which accepts a signature without the father's name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case setup offered in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 20's claim that "ראובן בן" / "יעקב עד" leaves neither half as a complete signature.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: "יעקב עד" matches the משנה's approved format of name plus "witness", so it should count as a valid signature for the second גט.

steps.title: The word "witness" is not written
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is one where the word "עד" is not written. So the second half is just a bare name, and that is not a valid signature.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where "witness" is not written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case. The word "עד" is missing, so the half under the second גט is only a name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה approves "So-and-so, witness", and the word "witness" is what turns a name into a signature. Without it, "יעקב" alone does not count, so the second גט has no valid signature from this pair.

keyTerms.meaning: Is written
Witness: the word added after a name to mark it as a signature

phrases.english: Where "witness" is not written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "יעקב עד" appears under the second גט, matching the משנה's valid format.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only "יעקב" appears, with no "עד", so it is not a valid signature.

steps.title: Even with "witness" written, we know it is not יעקב's signature
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: even if "עד" is written, we know that this signature does not belong to someone named יעקב. It is the end of ראובן בן יעקב's signature, so it cannot serve as a separate signature for the second גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: really, the case is where "witness" is written. But we know that this signature is not יעקב's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer. It allows that "עד" is written, but says we know no witness named יעקב signed here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer depended on a missing word. This answer works even with every word in place. A signature only counts if it is really the signature of a witness. Since we know "יעקב עד" is just the tail of ראובן's full name, it is not anyone's own signature, so it cannot validate the second גט.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces a second, alternative answer
Actually / really: keeps the original case and answers it another way
We know
Signature

steps.whatToRemember: A signature counts only if it really belongs to a witness. A piece of a stretched signature cannot be split off to act as a separate signature, either because "עד" is missing or because we know no יעקב signed.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
actually, it is where "witness" is written,
but where we know about this signature
that it is not Yaakov's.
phrases.notes: He means it is really the end of "ראובן בן יעקב", not a separate person named יעקב signing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to Step 21, without needing the missing-word setup of Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative answer: known facts about the signer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With "עד" written, "יעקב עד" should count as a valid signature.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since we know no יעקב signed, the words are only part of ראובן's signature and validate nothing on their own.
